terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo chunks the Saltmarsh handbook with your code.

tasks.title: Split text into whole-word chunks
tasks.description:
Implement `chunkText(text, size)` in `src/chunk.ts`. It returns a `string[]` of chunks:

- Words are separated by any whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks). A chunk is its words joined by single spaces.
- Fill each chunk with as many words as fit in `size` characters, then start the next chunk.
- Never cut a word. A single word longer than `size` becomes a chunk on its own.
- Blank text gives `[]`.

The check calls `chunkText` with no overlap on handbook articles and on short edge cases (messy whitespace, a very long word, blank text) and compares the chunks.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the error for chunkText.
Split the text into words and drop the empty ones.
Walk the words, adding each to the current chunk while it still fits.
Run the demo again and check no chunk is longer than 80 characters.
hints: Work with a list of words, not with character positions. Then a word can never be cut.
A chunk's length is the sum of its word lengths plus one space between each pair of words.
Start a new chunk when the current length + 1 + the next word's length is more than size. A chunk always takes at least its first word, even when that word alone is too long.

tasks.title: Overlap neighbouring chunks
tasks.description:
Add the `overlap` parameter to `chunkText(text, size, overlap = 0)`.

- After a chunk, the next chunk starts by repeating the last words of that chunk, as many as fit in `overlap` characters (counting single spaces between them). Then it fills up to `size` as before.
- Never carry the whole previous chunk, so every chunk starts at least one word later than the one before.
- Stop once a chunk ends with the last word of the text.
- Throw an `Error` when `size` is below 1, `overlap` is negative, or `overlap` is not smaller than `size`.

The check compares your chunks on handbook articles and small word lists, makes sure the function always finishes, and tries the invalid settings.
nextSteps: Validate the arguments at the top of the function.
After building a chunk, work out which word the next chunk starts from.
Walk backwards from the end of the chunk while the carried words still fit in overlap.
Run the demo and compare the 80 and 80/20 outputs.
hints: Keep a start index into the words list. Each chunk is words from start up to some end.
Walking backwards from the chunk's end, count the carried length the same way you count a chunk: word lengths plus single spaces.
The next start must stay greater than the current start. Stop walking back one word before you reach it, and stop the loop when end reaches the last word.

tasks.title: Keep where each chunk came from
tasks.description:
Implement `chunkDocs(docs, size, overlap = 0)` in `src/chunk.ts`. It chunks every document with `chunkText` and returns a flat `Chunk[]` in document order. Each chunk is:

```ts
{ id: 'weather#2', source: 'weather', index: 2, text: '...' }
```

- `source` is the document's `id`.
- `index` is the chunk's position inside its own document, starting at 0 for every document.
- `id` is `'<source>#<index>'`, unique across the whole handbook.
- A document with empty text has no chunks.

The check uses a few hidden documents and the full handbook, and type-checks `src/chunk.ts`.
nextSteps: Call chunkText once for each document.
Turn each chunk string into a Chunk object with its metadata.
Flatten the per-document lists into one list.
Run the demo and read the chunk counts per document.
hints: The array method that maps and flattens in one step fits this well.
The second argument of a map callback is the position, which is exactly the index you need.
For each doc, map the strings chunkText gives you to objects, building the id from the doc's id, a # and the position.
